question: Which of the following instruments did Sheik Chinna Moulana, a famous instrumentalist from India, play?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Nadhaswaram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sheik Chinna Moulana** popularly known as **Sheik**, was a **prominent nadhaswaram player** in the tradition of Carnatic. He was felicited by the Madras Music Academy's **Sangeetha Kalanidhi** in **1998**
 
• Nadhaswaram__ is a double-reed wind instrument from South India.
 
• It is used as a traditional classical instrument in Tamilnadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, and Kerala.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• The____ ghaṭam__ is a percussion instrument used in various repertoires across India.
 
• It's a variant played in Punjab and known as gharha as it is a part of Punjabi folk traditions.
 
• Its analogue in Rajasthan is known as the madga and pani mataqa.
 
• The ghatam is one of the most ancient percussion instruments of India.
 
• __The mridangam__ is a percussion instrument of ancient origin.
 
• It is the primary rhythmic accompaniment in a Carnatic music ensemble.
 
• In Dhrupad, a modified version, the pakhawaj, is the primary percussion instrument.
 
• A related instrument is the Kendang, played in Maritime Southeast Asia.
 
• A tabla is a pair of twin-hand drums from the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Since the 18th century, tabla has been the principal percussion instrument in Hindustani classical music, where it may be played solo, as accompaniment with other instruments and vocals, and as a part of larger ensembles.
